goal-r1-f1.rationale: AC-15 IS legitimately anchored to the PRD's goal Outcome surfaces (c) chat-line summary citing the new entry's id and (d) zero silent failures (PRD line 135 explicitly: '(Verifies the goal Outcome surface (c) — chat-line summary citing the new entry's id; goal surface (d) — zero silent failures.)'). Option (b) is the right calibration: keep T15 (the chat-line summary is one cross-cutting contract worth tracking explicitly) but reshape the coverage-matrix row and Anchor line so the goal-anchored trace is observable.

goal-r1-f2.rationale: The values-that-look-like-defaults case is exactly the binary-boundary failure Goal-Driven Reviewer is meant to catch. Three retro-only fields can all hold default-shaped values (`actual_hours: 0` declined, `regressions_caught: {count:0, descriptions:[]}`, `escaped_issues: {count:0, descriptions:[], blast_radii:[]}`) and a fresh agent cannot tell those apart from 'no retro yet'. Reusing `superseded_by_retro: true` (set by T4's supersede-write) as the single-boolean existence signal makes T9's existence-check binary on a value the retro write provably toggles, and composes cleanly with the cross-skill schema dependency (T4's runtime-branch already refuses if the field is absent).
goal-r1-f2.revision_applied: T9 acceptance sharpened to bind 'existing retro' to the single boolean `superseded_by_retro: true`; coverage-matrix R9 row left unchanged (T9 still satisfies R9). T9 Notes line updated: '`superseded_by_retro: true` is the binary signal a retro fired; T4's supersede-write is the only path that flips it from `false` to `true`.'

simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: The chat-line summary contract IS a cross-cutting emit-on-exit rule across seven exit surfaces, AND the AC-15 verification it enables is one of the goal Outcome surfaces ((c) chat-line summary citing the new entry's id; (d) zero silent failures) named in the PRD Goal narrative directly. Folding the contract into seven per-task acceptances would split AC-15 verification across seven tasks AND lose the cross-cutting contract surface — a future change to the summary line format would have to be applied seven times instead of once, AND a Goal-Driven re-review would have to re-verify each task individually rather than reading one task's acceptance. The 002-develop-skill Gate 3 push-back precedent (simplicity-r1-f1: T5/T5b split kept) bites here in the same direction: simplicity at the task layer cannot override traceability anchored in a load-bearing cross-cutting contract. The dependency-list of seven tasks is not a signal of over-decomposition — it is a signal that AC-15's verification surface is exactly seven exit paths, AND tracking that as one task is the surgical-changes-compliant shape (the 'flag any required cross-cutting work' clause). Goal-Driven's goal-r1-f1 acceptance just sharpened T15's coverage-matrix row to make the goal-anchoring explicit; dropping T15 now would unwind the resolution that finding just landed.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: none — push-back; T15 retained as a distinct task tracking the cross-cutting AC-15 / Goal Outcome (c)+(d) contract. T15's coverage-matrix row carries the goal-anchored exception per goal-r1-f1; the per-task tasks (T1, T2, T4, T9, T10, T13, T14) cite their respective summary/refusal lines but do not duplicate AC-15's verification surface.

da-r1-f1.rationale: The (accept-and-ship + amend with kind:note) cross-product was indeed unhandled. T12's unconditional-elevation-prompt logic and T10's conditional-on-addendum-shape logic collide on the amend-of-accept-and-ship case; the task list did not pin which dominates. Pinning to once-per-original-retro-only firing for T12's unconditional logic (and following R6's two-condition rule on subsequent amends per T10 logic) is the deterministic shape that avoids re-prompting the user on every amend AND keeps the original retro's `decision_log_links` capture intact.
